title: Apple Is Considering Something It Hasn't Done in 15 Years. Here's What Investors Need to Know.
excerpt: Apple may be ready to get back into the server business.
content_html:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) is reportedly considering a big move that could reshape the company. The Information reported on Wednesday that the iPhone maker was considering developing its own artificial intelligence server, which would be Apple's first activity in the enterprise server market since 2011.

The proposal would combine Apple's custom silicon with networking technology supplied by Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) to develop AI servers that could be offered with either two or four M8 Ultra chips, which are Apple's top-performing processors, and geared specifically for AI inference.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Such a move, the first major action under new CEO John Ternus, would signal that Apple is ready to invest in AI architecture to use its custom-made chips in products beyond its consumer devices, which would be a significant shift in company strategy.

Image source: Getty Images.

Here's what we know about Apple's proposed servers

In its proposed partnership with Nvidia, Apple would use Nvidia's NVLink Fusion technology to connect its M8 Ultra chips to operate in its servers. NVLink is a high-speed chip-to-chip technology that allows graphics processing units (GPUs) to send data directly to one another. It includes specialized memory that works with custom AI chips to work with Nvidia data center systems.

Nvidia says its fourth-generation NVLink technology transmits data up to 900 gigabytes per second, which is 7 times the bandwidth of the connections used in conventional x86 servers. According to The Information's report, Apple staff believe that Nvidia's technology offers the best available technology, but Apple's proposed server could be developed without NVLink. Ternus, who was Apple's senior vice president of hardware engineering before becoming CEO this month, backed the initiative when it was suggested a year ago, the report said.

Apple hasn't been in the server hardware business since 2011, when it discontinued its Xserve line and shifted its resources toward standard hardware and consumer devices.

Apple's AI strategy to date has been focused on consumers and devices

In recent years, Apple faced a lot of criticism for not investing more in AI infrastructure. The other members of the Magnificent Seven grouping -- Microsoft, Tesla, Meta Platforms, Amazon, and Alphabet -- are all spending hundreds of billions on GPUs, CPUs, connectivity, memory, and data centers to develop their own cloud computing networks or specialized AI platforms. (The final member of the Magnificent Seven is Nvidia, which is the top AI chip supplier.)
